fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Charlatans, Intention, and What Makes Orgonite Work", "body": "Chance opens with a candid worry that subtle energy devices attract charlatans, so he says intention and the maker matter as much as the object. He describes a vendor tent of novelty orgonite shaped like movie characters that left him uneasy, then contrasts it with the pieces Mitch sent, which he says gave him a tingling charge along his spine. Mitch stresses that substance matters, saying a properly made device should be roughly half metal and half resin, and that he considers most of the orgonite sold in Sedona crystal shops poorly made."}, {"title": "Mitch Reads the Sky", "body": "Mitch argues that some of the clouds overhead are not ordinary weather, saying he watches the sky closely and that the wind has little to do with how certain hazes gather and curl around the sun. He ties what he sees to what he calls DOR, a Reichian term he translates as deadly orgone radiation, and says towers, phones, LED lights and smart devices electrify the atmosphere. He also says he noticed chemtrail activity rising before new and full moons. By his own account these are patterns and correlations he has found, and he says he does not have all the answers."}, {"title": "The Sun, the Food Chain, and Chembusters", "body": "Chance reflects that every meal is a chain of events that began at the sun, so a dimmed sun, in his telling, would weaken every link of the biosphere and not only our vitamin D. Mitch agrees, calling the sun the source of life and saying he believes some force opposes the life cycle itself. He describes aiming his chembusters at what he calls electrosmog and chemtrails, and says the haze breaks down, the sun reappears and a gust of wind follows. He presents this as something he has seen repeatedly, and he is candid that he cannot explain every part of it."}, {"title": "Reich, Arizona, and the Toolkit", "body": "Mitch calls Wilhelm Reich's Contact with Space the best doorway into Reich's work and says Reich's time in Arizona is part of why he moved to Sedona. He lays out his toolkit: tower busters made of resin, metal shavings and quartz, and earth pipes buried facing downward in the desert and mountains. As proof he offers a freezer water test that he says produces a vortex pattern and a garden test he says speeds growth, then reads a Reich passage insisting no authority can decide tomorrow's knowledge. He urges listeners to research and experiment rather than take his word."}, {"title": "From Skeptic to Solution Focused", "body": "Mitch says he set out to prove orgonite wrong and thought it stupid at first. He recounts scattering devices around Taos during a drought, and Chance reports daily rain since he buried an earth pipe, which Mitch answers with an educated guess about shaking up the local EMF bubble. Mitch insists orgonite is no band-aid for electromagnetic exposure, urging people to switch devices off at night and hardwire their internet, and says he is not a doctor and will not give medical advice. Closing the hour he calls the solution surprisingly simple but demanding. In the outro Chance urges listeners to be kind to their older selves."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Mitch Kohl is a creator of orgone technology who gifts his devices to the Earth, in an effort to undo the ongoing damage to the environment from geoengineering, the EMF frequency fence, and overhead chemical spraying. In this show we discuss Reich (who coined the term Orgone), proofs of orgonite's effects, the HAARP program and how it's disguised, chembusters (tech to dissolve chemtrails in the sky), and much more.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "HAARP, Word Magic, and the Network in Our Pockets", "body": "Chance opens with some word magic on HAARP's name, reading Aurora as our aura and wondering what is being researched and programmed. Mitch says the Alaska facility was officially decommissioned and handed to a university, which he calls a lie, and that it was upgraded into the 3G and 4G networks. He describes HAARP as playing with frequencies off the ionosphere and argues the network is now bigger than any one site because people carry it in their pockets. Chance relays a secondhand video he says he cannot back up, and Mitch remarks that anything easy to find is probably there because someone wanted it seen."}, {"title": "Disguised Towers and Where They Cluster", "body": "Mitch walks through slides of equipment he says is disguised: boxes in alleyways painted to match buildings, a tower he says sits inside a church, and thick flagpoles he is sure hide antennas. He claims towers cluster around prisons, schools, hospitals, reservoirs and factory farms, places he calls energy generators of negative emotion, though he notes one church photo came from someone using an EMF meter. His end boss is Nexrad weather radar, which he says he has found six of in Arizona where the official count is four, and which his network has targeted."}, {"title": "Gifting, Nerve, and the Cloaking Device", "body": "On gifting, Mitch says stealth comes naturally and that almost nobody notices a person spinning a heavy chembuster in a driveway. He describes a cloaking device he carries, a knotted quartz point pulsed by a small generator, which he says throws off what he calls psychic attacks, while admitting some listeners will raise an eyebrow. He concedes the work can stir fear of arrest and calls the work as much psychic as physical. Later both men trade stories of black helicopters and uncanny strangers, which Mitch likens to Agent Smith checking in."}, {"title": "Water, Rain, and the Life Cycle", "body": "Mitch says the orgone community's rule of thumb is a quarter-mile range per device, with earth pipes doing better because they use ground conductivity and moisture. He guesses that towers often sit above water and advises busting them before digging when water runs short. Rain, in his telling, de-ionizes and cleanses the air, and he praises collected rainwater as especially structured. Chance describes grounding barefoot in a downpour, which he says helps him flush what he calls DOR. Mitch also shares colorful halos from his first week in Arizona and reads them as frequencies colliding."}, {"title": "Reich, Radiation, and Free Energy", "body": "Mitch recounts Reich's Oranur experiment as he understands it, saying radium inside an accumulator concentrated what Reich called DOR, and argues Reich's real offense was linking life energy to nuclear radiation. He says he is experimenting with radioactive material on a very small scale and is convinced, though he has not reverse engineered it, that orgone could unlock free energy. Mitch stops short of claiming orgonite neutralizes radioactivity. Chance wonders about older heaters powered by radium and recalls his earlier fear of Fukushima. Mitch points listeners to Reich's books, including Contact with Space and Ether, God and Devil, and Chance floats a Reich and nukes episode for next time."}]
